questions.text: User Financial Literacy Assessment - SSA: Document baseline financial literacy of mobile money users: (1) Prior banking experience (% of users previously banked); (2) Digital literacy (can users navigate USSD menus?); (3) Financial concepts understanding (interest, fees, savings, credit); (4) Numeracy levels (can users calculate fees, balances?); (5) Scam awareness (do users recognize fraud attempts?); (6) PIN security understanding (do users protect PINs?); (7) Skills gap analysis (what training needed?).
questions.evidence_required: Financial literacy surveys, Banking experience data, Digital literacy assessments, Financial concepts testing, Numeracy assessments, Scam awareness studies, Skills gap analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Many users first-time formal financial service users. Digital literacy low. Financial concepts unfamiliar. Scams common (users vulnerable). PIN sharing common (security risk).

questions.text: User-Technology Fit for Mobile Money: Assess match between user capabilities and mobile money interface: (1) Is USSD interface appropriate for user skill level?; (2) Can illiterate users use service (voice, visual aids)?; (3) Can elderly users navigate menus?; (4) Works on devices users have (feature phones)?; (5) Language support (English, French, local languages)?; (6) Accessibility for disabled users (visual, hearing impairments)?; (7) Shared device scenarios (multiple family members using same phone).
questions.evidence_required: User testing with target demographics, Accessibility testing, Device compatibility testing, Language support verification, Shared device scenario testing
questions.africa_specific_notes: USSD not intuitive (need training). Illiterate users need voice/visual. Elderly struggle with menus. Feature phones dominant. Local languages essential. Shared devices common (privacy risk).

questions.text: Financial Knowledge Requirements for Safe Usage: Assess financial knowledge needed to use mobile money safely: (1) Understanding fees (can users calculate total cost?); (2) Understanding interest (for credit/loans); (3) Understanding exchange rates (for cross-border); (4) Recognizing scams (fake agents, phishing); (5) Protecting PINs (not sharing, changing regularly); (6) Checking balances (verifying transactions); (7) Knowledge gaps and training needs.
questions.evidence_required: Financial knowledge assessments, Fee calculation testing, Interest understanding, FX comprehension, Scam recognition testing, PIN security practices, Training needs analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Users often don't understand fees (hidden costs). Interest concepts unfamiliar. FX rates confusing. Scams sophisticated (users vulnerable). PIN sharing cultural norm (must change behavior).

questions.text: User Financial Literacy Training - SSA: Describe comprehensive financial literacy program: (1) Training mode (in-person essential, agent-led, community sessions); (2) Language (local languages, not just English/French); (3) Training materials (visual, video, printed - not just online); (4) Trainer qualifications (financial knowledge + local context); (5) Training content (USSD navigation, fees, security, scam prevention); (6) Hands-on practice (users practice transactions); (7) Ongoing support (refresher training, help resources).
questions.evidence_required: Training curriculum, Trainer qualifications, Training materials (visual, local language), Training delivery data, Hands-on practice documentation, Ongoing support programs
questions.africa_specific_notes: In-person training essential (digital literacy low). Local language mandatory. Visual materials critical (low literacy). Agent-led training effective (trusted, accessible). Scam prevention essential.

questions.text: Agent Training & Certification: Ensure agents are competent to serve users: (1) Initial training (USSD, transactions, customer service, fraud prevention); (2) Ongoing training (new features, regulatory changes, scam trends); (3) Certification requirements (must pass test to become agent?); (4) Training quality (qualified trainers, comprehensive curriculum); (5) Agent knowledge assessment (regular testing); (6) Customer service training (handling complaints, assisting users); (7) Fraud prevention training (detecting fake users, protecting liquidity).
questions.evidence_required: Agent training curriculum, Certification procedures, Ongoing training programs, Knowledge assessment results, Customer service training, Fraud prevention training
questions.africa_specific_notes: Agents = frontline (must be competent). Many agents low education. Training must be practical (hands-on). Fraud prevention critical (agents vulnerable). Customer service essential (users trust agents).

questions.text: Training Effectiveness Measurement - Mobile Money: Demonstrate training actually works: (1) Pre/post training assessments (knowledge gained?); (2) Service adoption rates (are trained users using mobile money?); (3) Correct usage rates (are users using safely, correctly?); (4) User confidence levels (do users feel competent?); (5) Retention over time (do users remember 3-6 months later?); (6) Fraud victimization rates (does training reduce scams?); (7) User outcomes (does training lead to better financial health?).
questions.evidence_required: Pre/post assessments, Adoption tracking, Usage correctness audits, Confidence surveys, Retention studies, Fraud victimization data, Outcome measurements
questions.africa_specific_notes: Training effectiveness critical (resources scarce). Must show training leads to safe usage, not just knowledge. Fraud reduction key metric. Financial health outcomes important.

questions.text: Merchant & SME Financial Training: Competence building for business users: (1) Transaction verification (how to spot fake payment SMS); (2) Merchant portal usage (reconciling accounts, downloading statements); (3) Liquidity management for business (managing cash vs e-float); (4) Fraud prevention for merchants (common merchant scams); (5) Customer assistance (helping customers pay); (6) Record keeping (integrating mobile money with books).
questions.evidence_required: Merchant training materials, Fraud prevention guides, Portal usage tutorials
questions.africa_specific_notes: Merchants often targeted by fake SMS scams. Need specific training on verification and liquidity.

questions.text: User Support Channels - Mobile Money SSA: Provide accessible, multi-channel support: (1) Phone support (toll-free, local language, 24/7); (2) SMS support (for simple queries); (3) USSD support (help menus within USSD); (4) Agent support (in-person assistance); (5) WhatsApp support (for smartphone users); (6) Branch support (physical locations in cities); (7) Response time SLAs (critical <1 hour, general <4 hours).
questions.evidence_required: Support channel documentation, Language support matrix, 24/7 availability proof, Response time SLA data, Agent support procedures, Branch locations
questions.africa_specific_notes: Phone support critical (many users no internet). Local language essential. 24/7 needed (money emergencies). Agent support most accessible (in-person). Fast response critical (money urgent).

questions.text: Issue Resolution Capacity - Mobile Money: Ensure support can resolve user issues: (1) Self-service troubleshooting (USSD help menus, IVR); (2) Agent troubleshooting (agents can resolve common issues); (3) Call center troubleshooting (phone support can diagnose, resolve); (4) Escalation procedures (complex issues escalated to specialists); (5) Transaction reversal capability (failed transactions reversed quickly); (6) Account recovery (locked accounts, forgotten PINs); (7) Issue resolution tracking (are problems actually solved?).
questions.evidence_required: Self-service tools, Agent troubleshooting training, Call center capabilities, Escalation procedures, Reversal processes, Account recovery procedures, Resolution tracking metrics
questions.africa_specific_notes: Self-service limited (low digital literacy). Agents critical for troubleshooting. Transaction reversals must be fast (users panic). Account recovery essential (forgotten PINs common).

questions.text: Platform Learning from User Feedback - Mobile Money: Demonstrate continuous improvement: (1) User feedback collection (surveys, complaints, focus groups); (2) Agent feedback integration (agents report user issues); (3) Feedback analysis (what are pain points?); (4) Product improvements (what changes made based on feedback?); (5) User communication (are users told about improvements?); (6) User advisory boards (do users have voice in decisions?); (7) Fraud pattern analysis (learning from scam attempts).
questions.evidence_required: Feedback mechanisms, Agent feedback integration, Analysis reports, Product improvement logs, User communication, Advisory boards, Fraud pattern analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: User feedback critical for improvement. Agent feedback valuable (frontline insights). Fraud patterns evolve (must adapt). User communication builds trust. Advisory boards emerging.

questions.text: Knowledge Transfer & Local Capacity Building - Financial Services: Build long-term local capacity: (1) Local hiring (how many local staff vs expats?); (2) Skills transfer (are local staff trained for senior roles?); (3) Agent capacity building (training agents to support users); (4) Financial literacy ecosystem (supporting local educators); (5) Regulatory capacity building (supporting regulators); (6) Local partner development (working with local banks, MFIs); (7) Sustainability plan (can local team run platform if vendor exits?).
questions.evidence_required: Local hiring data, Skills transfer programs, Agent capacity building, Financial literacy support, Regulatory engagement, Partner development, Sustainability plan
questions.africa_specific_notes: Local capacity building critical for sustainability. Can't rely on expats long-term. Agent capacity essential. Financial literacy ecosystem important. Regulatory capacity building valued.

questions.text: Agent POS Device Support Infrastructure: Ensure agent devices can be maintained: (1) Local technician training (can local technicians repair POS devices?); (2) Repair documentation (visual guides, local language); (3) Spare parts availability (local inventory, lead times); (4) Repair cost (affordable for agents?); (5) Warranty claim process (accessible, fast); (6) Device replacement program (if repair not possible); (7) Alternative devices (can agents use smartphones as backup?).
questions.evidence_required: Technician training programs, Repair documentation, Spare parts inventory, Repair pricing, Warranty procedures, Replacement programs, Alternative device options
questions.africa_specific_notes: Agent POS devices critical (no device = no service). Local repair capacity essential. Spare parts often stuck in customs. Repair must be affordable. Smartphone backup useful.

questions.text: Agent Liquidity Management Infrastructure: Assess agent liquidity support systems: (1) E-float provision (how do agents get e-float? cost? speed?); (2) Cash management (how do agents get/deposit physical cash?); (3) Bank relationships (do agents have bank accounts? accessible?); (4) Super-agent network (do super-agents support smaller agents?); (5) Liquidity forecasting (can agents predict liquidity needs?); (6) Emergency liquidity (what if agent runs out of cash/e-float?); (7) Liquidity costs (fees for rebalancing).
questions.evidence_required: E-float provision procedures, Cash management systems, Bank relationship documentation, Super-agent network, Forecasting tools, Emergency liquidity procedures, Liquidity fee structures
questions.africa_specific_notes: Liquidity = biggest agent challenge. E-float provision must be fast, affordable. Cash management difficult (security, transport). Bank access limited (rural areas). Super-agents critical.

questions.text: Financial Services Ecosystem Integration: Assess integration with broader financial ecosystem: (1) Banking system integration (can users link bank accounts?); (2) Microfinance integration (loan disbursement, repayment via mobile money); (3) Insurance integration (micro-insurance via mobile money); (4) Savings products (can users save via mobile money?); (5) Credit products (mobile money-based credit); (6) Investment products (can users invest via mobile money?); (7) Interoperability (can users transact across providers?).
questions.evidence_required: Bank integration documentation, MFI partnerships, Insurance integration, Savings products, Credit products, Investment products, Interoperability agreements
questions.africa_specific_notes: Mobile money = gateway to financial services. Bank integration weak but growing. MFI integration important (credit access). Insurance emerging. Savings products critical. Interoperability limited.

scoring_notes: Layer 4 (Competence) for Financial Services in Sub-Saharan Africa: Financial literacy cannot be assumed - many first-time formal financial service users. Agent training critical (frontline service delivery). Support must be accessible (phone, local language, 24/7). Liquidity management = biggest agent challenge.
